title: SAML 1.1
heading: SAML 1.1
sub: The two browser profiles, and the SAML responder behind one of them
lead: This service issues SAML 1.1 assertions through three doors, and this is the newest of them: the browser profiles, where a person signs in and an assertion reaches a relying party. The other two are {wsfed}, which wraps the same assertion in a wresult, and {wstrust}, which returns one in an RSTR. All three call one builder, so an attribute configured on /admin/saml-attributes appears in all three.
sso: the inter-site transfer service — SAML 1.1's name for what SAML 2.0 calls the Single Sign-On service
responder: the SAML responder, over SOAP. Resolves artifacts, returns assertions by AssertionID, and answers AttributeQuery and AuthenticationQuery — the attribute authority half of SAML 1.1
metadata: signed metadata. A SAML 2.0 metadata document describing a SAML 1.1 identity provider, which is what every relying party actually consumes
rp: a mock relying party, to exercise both profiles and see the checks
different: What makes it different from SAML 2.0
noRequest: No request message. No AuthnRequest, so the relying party never identifies itself, never asks for a binding, a NameID format or an authentication context, and never receives an error — there is nothing to answer.
noSlo: No Single Logout. It arrived with SAML 2.0.
spellings: Different spellings throughout. AssertionID not ID, an Issuer attribute not an element, a status code that is a QName not a URI, AudienceRestrictionCondition not AudienceRestriction, and a signature that goes LAST in an assertion and FIRST in a response.
artifact: A 42-byte artifact, type 0x0001, where SAML 2.0's is 44 bytes and type 0x0004.
tryIt: Try it at the mock relying party
